title: Choose the visual world for Blabbit's site
question: The roll assigned the Freeware Desktop world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Freeware Desktop
options.lineage: Classic Mac OS system software and the 90s freeware scene
options.thesis: The site is a Mac desktop you dictate into, the way free Mac software was always handed around.
options.viewport: A full-screen desktop with a real menu bar. You hold a big ⌥ Space keycap and words type into a TextEdit-like window, beside a Read Me window saying 'Free. Open source. On your Mac.' and the Download icon.
options.risk: Reads as retro cosplay if the modern speed story (75 ms, Apple Silicon) isn't just as loud.

raised.raise: One hot color only: safety orange marks 'live' (holding the key, recording) and nothing else.
Motion has mass: windows, the cursor and the level meter move with GSAP spring ballistics, never instant or linear.
A strict whole-unit grid: windows and icons snap to an 8px desktop grid on every breakpoint.

options.label: Shorthand Pad
options.lineage: Gregg shorthand notebooks and court stenography
options.thesis: Stenographers wrote speech as fast as it was spoken. Blabbit does it for free.
materials: pen strokes that morph into type
options.viewport: A giant steno pad page where shorthand strokes draw themselves and resolve into typed words as you scroll.
options.risk: Close to the paper-and-serif editorial look many AI sites land on, and the Mac isn't in it.

options.label: Creator Hardware Bench
options.thesis: Blabbit as an instrument with one orange key: hold it and talk.
options.viewport: A gunmetal device fills the screen. The orange ⌥ Space key is pressable, and the amber screen types your words as the knob scrubs through models.
options.case: Wins clarity (the key IS the product), loses general Mac users, who don't know this gear culture.
options.risk: Can feel like a hardware product people will try to buy.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: Black and white pixels only: dithered windows and marching ants around the words you just said.
options.viewport: A one-bit desktop where dictated text appears in a window and gets selected with marching ants.
options.case: Holds audience identification; loses clarity, because pure one-bit hides the modern, fast app.
options.risk: Hard to read on phones, and it looks old rather than fast.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: A row of needles reacting to your voice.
options.viewport: A meter bridge that leans into the red as a sample phrase plays.
options.risk: About audio, not text; it misses the words appearing at the cursor.
options.case: Loses both: shows sound, not writing.
options.kept: Motion with mass and damping, never instant values.

options.label: Teletext Weather Mosaic
options.viewport: A P100 page with dictation as subtitle rows.
options.risk: Not a Mac, and unfamiliar to many.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.kept: One hot color reserved for the live state.

options.label: Gravity Rain Garden
options.viewport: A dusk garden of bent rain.
options.risk: Pure mood, and the product disappears.
options.kept: State shown as a physical law, not decoration.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark, glowy AI-app landing page, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline, two buttons, product mock below.
canonCard.risk: This is what the current site is, and what you called AI slop.
